The ad sales team is responsible for the advertising vision, development and growth of our largest advertising partnerships. The growing DoorDash ads business will quickly become the single best place for merchants and brands to market to local customers, in an ecosystem that benefits all parties.

As an Enterprise Associate - Ad Sales, you will manage, execute, and improve processes that accelerate growth of our ads and promotions offering and drive efficiency of our sales team. In this role, you will execute campaign contracts, setup, and billing while also analyzing reporting to drive campaign performance. You will work hand in hand with the Account Executive and clients to ensure seamless launch of all marketing campaigns. You will also work cross-functionally with account management, legal, revenue and accounting, and partner management teams to improve our tools and processes.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Be a founding member of the DoorDash Ads & Promos team

jobs.description: The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy. We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers. We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade. Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities. Job Summary: Reporting to the Sr. Director, Enterprise Quality, the Director, Enterprise Quality is a founding leader of PayPal’s new enterprise quality function. Today, quality is managed inconsistently across the company – standards differ from team to team, issues surface late, and feedback loops are broken. The Director helps change that: shaping the common standards and ways of working that make quality an enterprise discipline, and partnering across Product, Engineering, Design, Risk, Servicing, and Go-to-Market to build quality into how PayPal plans, builds, launches, and operates its products. Working across all three business units and enabling functions, the role concentrates – depending on focus – on defining the enterprise standards for quality, or on driving their adoption and adherence in the field. It is fundamentally an influence role: success comes through clarity, trust, and enablement rather than direct authority over business-unit roadmaps. Job Description: Essential Responsibilities: Lead the end-to-end design, analysis, and optimization of business processes to enhance efficiency, compliance, and effectiveness. Collaborate with cross-functional teams and senior leadership to align process improvements with organizational goals and strategic priorities. Identify, assess, and resolve complex business process challenges, driving sustainable improvements and measurable business outcomes. Oversee governance frameworks and ensure compliance with internal standards and external regulatory requirements. Leverage Lean, Six Sigma, or other methodologies to implement large-scale process improvement initiatives with significant impact on cost, quality, and productivity. Develop and implement performance management systems to monitor key process metrics, ensuring accountability and continuous optimization. Lead user acceptance testing and change management efforts to ensure adoption of improved processes and tools. Serve as a subject matter expert and mentor, coaching teams and leaders on process improvement best practices and methodologies. Establish and maintain documentation, standards, and best practices to promote operational consistency and scalability. Prepare and present detailed reports, insights, and recommendations to executive leadership on process performance and improvement opportunities. Minimum Qualifications: 10+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience. Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications : 10+ years of progressive experience in business operations, program or portfolio management, product operations, quality, corporate strategy, or risk and controls, including leading complex global initiatives. jobs.description: AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. The Data Center Capacity Delivery Asia-Pacific Controls Deployment and Service (DCCD APAC CDS) team delivers and services the control systems that ensure the health of AWS data centers. Operating across Australia & New Zealand, India, North Asia, and Southeast Asia, APAC CDS manages 41 leased/owned sites and supports global follow-the-sun operations. APAC CDS covers three core disciplines: deployments (control systems in new data centers), projects (capital improvement works at live sites), and service (control systems at live sites), with additional specializations in colocated sites, systems engineering, controls fleet, program management, and coordination. Being successful in our roles is not just about doing our jobs well, but also evolving and innovating. Change is the only constant, and applies to our customers, our roles, our team organization, our tools, and our mechanisms. To be successful in this team, you will also have: - Ability to thrive at the pace and scale of Amazon - Ability to work independently and manage multiple competing priorities - Ability and willingness to collaborate with peers around the globe, which may involve some participation in meetings at odd hours - Ability and willingness to travel domestically or globally as and when needed Controls Deployment & Service (CDS) Engineers deliver and support data center building automation systems, such as Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS). CDS Engineers work to deploy and service building automation systems, to ensure the health of our data centers. As a CDS Engineer, you may oversee deployment of a new BMS or EPMS as part of a new data center build, deliver projects to upgrade an existing data center owned or leased by Amazon, or deliver projects to upgrade colocated data centers with Amazon hardware. As a CDS Engineer, you may also be required to provide local servicing expertise to our fleet or data centers in your region, and occasionally assist with global support. Successfully working as a CDS Engineer will also require you to partner effectively with the many teams at Amazon that make our data center deployments and operations a success, including Construction, Commissioning, Critical Projects, Data Center Operations, Procurement, Program Management, Design, and Engineering teams, as well as maintaining strong relationships with our vendors. Our team is responsible for the development, integration, and deployment of electrical and mechanical control infrastructure for AWS data centers globally. As part of the Data Center Control Engineering Team, you will be part of a highly creative, efficient team tasked with tackling fascinating and challenging problems building and supporting control systems for AWS owned data centers within the APJC region and globally. The AWS Data Center Capacity Delivery Control team works on Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) that monitor and control critical infrastructure including HVAC equipment, chillers, air handling units, electrical distribution, UPS systems, and generators to maintain optimal data center operations. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop expertise in data center control systems engineering within one of the world's most innovative technology companies. You'll receive mentorship from industry-leading controls professionals, gain exposure to cutting-edge automation and monitoring systems, and contribute to projects that shape the future of cloud computing infrastructure.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1246dead-d30e-4c70-a1d3-ef7e5023d542/dd13138b-994f-4735-becb-eb8b2e863c8a/Clash%20of%20Clans%20_%20attack.png]

GREAT GAMES DESERVE CREATIVE THAT MAKES PEOPLE WANT TO PLAY THEM. WE’RE LOOKING FOR A MARKETING CREATIVE LEAD TO SHAPE THE FUTURE OF USER ACQUISITION CREATIVE ACROSS SUPERCELL’S PORTFOLIO OF LIVE AND NEW GAMES. BASED IN HELSINKI, YOU’LL LEAD AND DEVELOP OUR UA CREATIVE TEAM, SET THE STRATEGIC DIRECTION FOR THE DISCIPLINE, AND HELP US MAKE AMBITIOUS CREATIVE BETS THAT CONNECT OUR GAMES WITH PLAYERS WORLDWIDE.

This is a senior leadership role with broad ownership. You’ll work across games, franchises and creative formats—giving talented Creative Producers the context, trust and support to do their best work while building the strategies and systems that help us learn faster and raise the creative bar. You’ll partner closely with Marketing Leads, General Managers, Creative Leadership, game teams and global partners to decide where our creative can have the greatest impact.

About Creative Studio

Creative Studio is Supercell's in-house creative team, and this role sits at the heart of it. We're a small, cross-discipline group — Creative Producers, marketing artists, video artists, animators and AI pipeline specialists — embedded inside Marketing and working directly with game teams across the portfolio.

We're deliberately building capability in-house. Our animators, artists and editors sit close to the games, know the worlds intimately, and can go from idea to finished asset without a brief travelling through three companies first. External partners still matter — we work with agencies, production companies and specialist vendors for scale and specialist formats — but the strategy, the direction and the quality bar stay with us.

We're also early. Creative Studio was formed recently, and much of how it works is still being written. That's the opportunity in this role: you'll help decide how our internal talent is deployed, what we build ourselves versus buy, and what the operating model looks like as it matures.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1246dead-d30e-4c70-a1d3-ef7e5023d542/7a053edc-bf2e-4db4-85ee-5630e2b5d305/banner_narrow_customs.jpg]

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

- Lead and develop the UA Creative team. Lead, coach and inspire Creative Producers working across both live and new games. Build an environment where people have the autonomy, context and support to make strong decisions, take ownership and grow into future production leaders.

- Set the strategic direction for UA Creative. Own creative strategy across Supercell’s portfolio, developing playbooks, testing methodologies and repeatable frameworks that help teams identify opportunities, validate hypotheses and scale winning ideas.

- Shape creative across the player journey. Guide strategies spanning gameplay-based creative, playable ads, cinematic animation, App Store Optimization (ASO), interactive experiences, social-first creative and emerging formats—from early concept testing and soft launch through global launch and LiveOps.

- Own the UA Creative portfolio. Take a portfolio-wide view of investment across games, audiences, formats, channels and franchises. Help teams determine where to place ambitious creative bets, when to scale successful approaches and where experimentation can unlock something new.

- Turn games into compelling creative ideas. Champion a deep understanding of gameplay systems, player motivations and game design. Help teams find the mechanics, emotions, and stories that authentically represent our games while creating entertaining, culturally relevant, and performance-driven work.

- Drive prioritization and alignment. Partner with Marketing Leads, General Managers and Creative Leadership to connect UA Creative priorities with broader company and game objectives. Bring clarity when priorities compete, make thoughtful trade-offs and help teams stay focused on the opportunities with the greatest potential impact.

- Build ways of working that scale. Continuously improve how UA Creative is planned, prioritised, reviewed and delivered. Create systems that enable teams to move quickly without lowering the creative bar, and make sure insights and learnings travel effectively between games and teams.

- Find new ways to work across teams. Build the connections between Creative Studio, game teams, brand, ASO, franchise and our Animation Supervision team in Seoul. A lot of the biggest opportunities sit in the gaps between functions. Part of this role is spotting them and creating the working models that unlock them.

- Get the most from our internal creative talent. Work with our marketing artists, video artists and animators to make sure internal craft is pointed at the work where it makes the biggest difference. Decide what we own in-house, where we bring in partners, and how the two fit together.

- Build the pipelines behind the work. Creative capability isn't only people — it's the pipelines, tooling and asset systems that let a small team produce at scale. Partner with our AI pipeline specialists and creative technologists to build production workflows that speed up ideation, iteration and delivery, and make sure what we learn in one pipeline becomes something the whole studio can use.

- Champion franchise quality. Work closely with our Animation Supervision team in Seoul, game teams and external partners to ensure acquisition creative strengthens each franchise’s identity while continuing to evolve with players, cultures and platforms.

- Grow our creative ecosystem. Build strong relationships with agencies, production companies, AI partners and specialist vendors, using external expertise thoughtfully to complement our internal capabilities and expand what our teams can create. Over time, the goal is to do more of the highest-impact work in-house; with partners used for scale and specialist capability, not as a substitute of internal creative thinking.

WHAT YOU HAVE

- Extensive experience leading User Acquisition Creative, creative strategy or marketing production within mobile gaming, entertainment or consumer technology.

- A track record of leading, mentoring and developing high-performing Creative Producers, including helping others grow into broader leadership responsibilities.

- Demonstrated success setting creative direction beyond an individual project or campaign, with the judgement to influence priorities and investment across multiple teams, games or products.

- Experience building creative strategy frameworks, experimentation methodologies and scalable operating models that improve creative quality and marketing performance.

- Strong knowledge of UA Creative across gameplay-based assets, playable ads, animation, ASO, social-first creative and emerging acquisition formats.

- A deep understanding of mobile game design, player psychology and gameplay systems, and an ability to identify the mechanics and emotional hooks that can become compelling acquisition creative.

- Experience supporting games across their lifecycle, from concept validation and new-game incubation through soft launch, global launch and long-term LiveOps.

- Excellent judgement in ambiguous situations and the ability to prioritise across competing opportunities, stakeholders and business objectives without needing every decision prescribed.

- Experience partnering with Marketing Leads, General Managers and senior cross-functional leaders, influencing strategy and creating alignment around significant creative decisions.

- Experience collaborating effectively across globally distributed teams, animation studios and external creative partners.

- A passion for building exceptional teams and creating the conditions for others to produce the best work of their careers.

WOULD BE NICE IF YOU ALSO HAVE

- Experience shaping UA Creative strategy across a portfolio of multiple games or globally recognized entertainment franchises.

- Experience building or scaling an in-house creative team, including hands-on involvement in production pipelines, tooling, or asset systems.

- Experience connecting creative experimentation with performance insights and using those learnings to influence broader marketing strategy.

- Experience establishing new creative capabilities, workflows, or teams and evolving them as an organization scales.

- A strong perspective on how AI, new production technologies, and emerging creative formats can expand creative possibilities while maintaining quality and franchise integrity.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

- You’ll help make UA Creative a strategic advantage for Supercell. Our Creative Producers will have the clarity and autonomy to make excellent decisions, our game teams will have a trusted creative partner, and learnings from one game will make the whole portfolio stronger.

- You’ll raise our ambition while helping us make smart choices about where to focus. Success won’t simply mean producing more creative—it will mean building a team, strategy and operating model capable of consistently finding ideas that earn players’ attention and strengthen our games for the long term.

WHERE YOU'LL BE

- This role is based in Helsinki, Finland, at Supercell’s headquarters. You’ll work closely with teams and leaders across our global offices, including our Animation Supervision team in Seoul, as well as external creative partners around the world.

- Because the role has portfolio-wide and global responsibilities, you should be comfortable collaborating across locations and time zones and travelling when being together in person will make the work better.

WHY YOU'LL LOVE IT HERE

- At Supercell, small teams are trusted with a lot of responsibility. For this role, that means having meaningful ownership over how UA Creative evolves across our games rather than simply executing a predefined playbook.

- You’ll have the opportunity to build the team, challenge existing approaches, experiment with new ones and help decide where we place our biggest creative bets. We set a high bar, take risks, learn when things don’t work and share those learnings openly. And because the strongest ideas rarely belong to one person, you’ll be expected to lead with both conviction and humility—creating the conditions for talented people around you to succeed.

- Ultimately, this role is about helping great teams make creative worthy of great games—and helping those games find players who may love them for years.

–––

That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read.

Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page.

ABOUT SUPERCELL

Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices https://supr.cl/jd-offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. Our mission is to create great games https://supr.cl/jd-games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.

So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings https://supercell.com/en/news/learning-from-failures/, and killing lots of projects.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1246dead-d30e-4c70-a1d3-ef7e5023d542/0272a5b3-a7a2-4f1c-b97b-725eae66daf0/banner_narrow_people3.jpg]

HEY, YOU MIGHT LOVE IT HERE!

Independent cells and trust are at the core of our culture https://supr.cl/jd-why-you. But it takes more than that to make great games. We take good care of our people, providing them with the compensation, work environment, and resources they need to succeed while having fun along the way.

YOU ARE NOT YOUR JOB TITLE ™

BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION

RELOCATION? YES!

NOT SURE IF YOU SHOULD APPLY?

Many candidates with great skills and experience second-guess themselves. The bar is high, but if this role excites you, apply! We’re here to help you succeed. Also, we're happy to learn about any specific accommodations you may need to fully engage in our recruitment process.

About the Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.

This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale. This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.

You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process. You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.

The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring. You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.

In This Role, You Will

- Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop.

- Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions.

- Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use.

- Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity.

- Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments.

- Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions.

- Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not.

- Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

- Have 8+ years of experience in trust and safety operations, investigations, incident response, product operations, technical program management, or another high-judgment, data-heavy operational field.

- Have a track record as a scrappy generalist who can enter an unfamiliar problem, learn quickly, and deliver with limited structure or support.

- Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.

- Are technically fluent and hands-on with AI tools, dashboards, and data tooling, and can build or prototype practical solutions without waiting for a dedicated technical team.

- Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.

- Think in systems: you look beyond the immediate task and build approaches that can be repeated, measured, and operated by others.

- Exercise strong judgment in sensitive situations involving user impact, policy, legal risk, technical constraints, and business priorities.

- Communicate clearly and directly, especially in writing, and can drive decisions across teams without formal authority.

Nice to Have

- Experience in trust and safety, fraud, product safety, integrity, or another adversarial or high-severity risk domain.

- Experience moving a new or immature workflow from early investigation into stable, scaled operations.

- Experience supporting cloud platforms or deployment partnerships, enterprise products, product launches, connected devices, or other technically complex programs. Direct cloud experience is a plus, not a requirement.

- Familiarity with SQL, lightweight scripting, no-code tools, workflow automation, or AI-assisted development.

- Experience with vendor operations, quality programs, calibrations, or distributed operational teams.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the first hire for our Revenue Strategy & Operations team in Southeast Asia, you'll partner with sales leadership to plan and run our business across the region from Singapore, from the region's largest enterprises and business groups to its fastest‑growing technology companies.

You will be the trusted advisor to our regional sales leadership on how the business is planned and run, shaping how we invest across a set of very different markets while building the operational foundations to scale. Much of the work you will do yourself, hands‑on.

This role suits a structured thinker who is comfortable with ambiguity: you will often start from an open question, turn it into a clear recommendation, and get leaders who don't report to you aligned behind it.

You'll work closely with Strategy & Operations peers in Australia, Japan, Korea and India, with global Revenue Operations and Finance, and you'll use Claude every day to do the work of a much larger team.

You'll start as a senior individual contributor, with the opportunity to build and lead a small team as the region scales. You'll report to the head of Revenue Strategy & Operations for Asia‑Pacific (based in Sydney), work day to day alongside our sales leaders and team in Singapore, and travel regularly within the region.

Responsibilities

Go‑to‑Market Strategy

• Lead annual and quarterly go‑to‑market planning for the region with sales leadership and Finance — set targets, territories and sales capacity, and own the trade‑offs behind them.
• Set how we segment a multi‑country market and design territories, from large enterprises and business groups that operate across borders to fast‑growing technology companies.
• Align leadership on market prioritization and coverage — where we invest first, how we cover the rest — and revisit the call as the business grows.
• Shape how we go to market with partners and resellers — co‑selling, partner pipeline and joint planning — alongside our partnerships team.
• Give sales leadership an independent read of the business — performance, pipeline and consumption across markets — with the risks, the opportunities and a recommended course of action, early enough to act on.

Rhythm of the Business & Regional Leadership

• Own the operating rhythm of the region — weekly forecast and pipeline reviews, monthly and quarterly business reviews — and make it the place where decisions get made, not where reports get read.
• Represent the region with Revenue Operations, Sales Enablement, Finance, Marketing and Partnerships; keep its plans aligned with Asia‑Pacific and the company, and bring back what works elsewhere.
• Advise regional and Asia‑Pacific leadership through planning sessions, performance reviews and leadership updates — own the narrative, not just the numbers.
• Influence without authority: bring structure to ambiguous problems, build the case, and drive decisions across teams you don't manage.

Operations & Global Programs

• Own the region's commercial governance — account and territory decisions, planning inputs, data standards — working through our global Revenue Operations team, who own the CRM and sales systems.
• Land global programs, processes and tools in the region, and be the region's voice back to headquarters when something needs to change.
• Keep the commercial engine running smoothly across the multi‑country, multi‑stakeholder sales cycles typical of enterprise software in the region.

You may be a good fit if you have

Required qualifications

• 8-12 years of experience in B2B SaaS, cloud or enterprise software, including several years leading sales strategy, revenue operations or commercial go‑to‑market work as the advisor to a sales leader — ideally across more than one Southeast Asian market
• Structured thinking: a track record of taking ambiguous, open‑ended problems and turning them into options, a recommendation and a decision
• Analytical depth: you can get from raw data to a recommendation yourself, and you know which three numbers a leader needs to see
• You have owned annual planning, territory design, quota setting and business reviews for enterprise sales teams that cover several countries
• Hands‑on with Salesforce and data — reports, dashboards and your own analysis; you use the systems yourself rather than administer them
• Presence and judgement with senior sales leadership and C‑level stakeholders — including the confidence to give an unwelcome recommendation — and a record of getting decisions made across teams you don't manage
• Comfortable operating in ambiguity and at pace; you can build the process while running it
• A record of advising regional leadership on go‑to‑market strategy and getting the organization behind it
• Based in Singapore, with fluent English

Strong candidates may also have

• Management consulting experience (strategy or operations work), ideally combined with time in an operating role
• A track record of scaling sales organizations through 3x+ growth periods in B2B software, including expansion into new markets
• Experience building and leading a small team, or clear readiness to do so as the function scales
• Go‑to‑market experience with partners, resellers or cloud marketplaces in the region
• Experience in Chief of Staff or Business Operations roles supporting regional leadership
• Professional proficiency in one or more languages of the region, in addition to English

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.description: Project Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Come work at Amazon! As a member of Leo MAC-SW, you will be responsible for delivering embedded FW code running on ground networks on customer terminals and on satellites. Come and join the innovative and unique wireless project Leo. You would be focused on designing, developing and testing complete Leo-MAC FW. You will be a key member of a cross functional team of innovators, working on unique wireless technology that will enable millions of people to stay connected. Design, develop, integrate and bring up Leo-MAC FW components/drivers in a real-time embedded environment Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities * Working in a cross-functional environment to define multi-dimensional performance requirements (e.g., MIPs, memory BW) * Make performance and optimization trade-offs to meet end-to-end use case requirement * Build component use-cases/test-cases and debug your code in Leo embedded environment * Profile and execute the code on RTOS and/or bare-metal embedded environment * Contribute in defining services and functionalities delivered by your FW-subsystems * Define, document, test and debug your FW-HW interfaces * Familiarity with SW/FW best practices (e.g., clean architecture, refactoring, …)
